quote: I meant to write about death, only life came breaking in as usual.
source: Virginia Woolf, The Diary of Virginia Woolf, Volume Two: 1920 to 1924, the entry for 17 February 1922 (ed. Anne Olivier Bell, 1978)
note: Corrected the work. The sentence is not in A Writer’s Diary: a search of that 1953 selection finds it nowhere, and the entry Leonard Woolf printed for the day carries the review of Monday or Tuesday instead. It stands in the complete diary, volume two, under 17 February 1922.

evidence.where: Downloaded the full scanned text of A Writer’s Diary (Internet Archive item in.ernet.dli.2015.461396) and searched it: no hit for the phrase, and the 1922 selection begins at 15 February, with the 17 February entry running from the phenacetin dose to the Dial review. The following entry, 18 February, opens by saying her mind is once more distracted from the thought of death, which places the missing sentence in the unabridged entry for the 17th. The Yale Review essay by Edmund de Waal on the making of Mrs Dalloway quotes the sentence and dates it to February 1922; quotation references give 17 February 1922 and libquotes cites the 1920 to 1924 diary volume. The page of that volume was not seen.
evidence.edition: The Diary of Virginia Woolf, Volume Two: 1920 to 1924, ed. Anne Olivier Bell with Andrew McNeillie (Hogarth Press, 1978)

reason: The wording is Woolf’s and the date is corroborated, but the proposed work was wrong: the line was cut from Leonard Woolf’s 1953 selection, which I checked in full, and belongs to the complete diary. The dated entry is locator enough; no page is claimed because none was seen.
